sourceInformation.source: Demon Attack (1982), Imagic; an original game inspired by its fixed-screen shooting, swooping demons and splitting enemies.
sourceInformation.perspective: Orthographic front view of a 3D battlefield; horizontal player movement
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU preferred and WebGL 2 fallback, Three.js TSL, Rapier 0.19.3, Gamepad API, Web Audio API, WebRTC, AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.25.11
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded 3D geometry, thick ink outlines, coral/cyan/cream palette over midnight navy; no external art assets.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks for wingbeats and thrusters; simulation-driven swoops, dives, boss phases and procedural particles.
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated 112 BPM synth music at 10% default volume, oscillator/noise sound effects and formant-filtered Animalese-style gibberish; no audio files.
sourceInformation.online: Host-authoritative 1–4 player AI Hub shared-world co-op; standalone two-player WebRTC capsule pairing; two-player couch co-op.
sourceInformation.testing: 37 grouped automated checks: deterministic Rapier collisions and a full seven-encounter AI playthrough, offline WebGPU startup, keyboard/mouse, standard gamepad emulation, phone touch, audio sample analysis, real two-page WebRTC, and four AI Hub scenarios including 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% loss, host departure and a host without a player seat. Visual and four-copy stress checks use the same renderer’s WebGL 2 backend. Physical hardware, human listening and WAN NAT traversal are unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No source or general internet research; native model knowledge only. Read the user-supplied AI Hub protocol and pinned dependency source for implementation; no internet search.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 5 game issues found and fixed: inline-script packaging, missed brief ability taps, phone-title overflow, HUD overlap and renderer startup recovery. Three test-runner/fixture issues were also corrected.
2 blocked play in affected builds or environments: broken inline-script packaging and failed renderer initialization.

The seeded full-game AI playthrough using real Rapier collisions. It completed every encounter, all enemy mechanics, both boss transitions, pickups, dashes and Encores; the Hub harness separately checked multiplayer lifecycle.

Software WebGPU screenshots were least useful: canvas capture was blank despite active simulation and renderer frames. The same scenes captured through the WebGL 2 backend were useful for composition.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL supplied consistent quantized lighting across procedural models; AnimationMixer made reusable wingbeats and thrusters straightforward.

Brief input polling and minified-script embedding initially needed corrections. Software WebGPU startup across many iframe lifetimes required recovery through the renderer’s WebGL 2 backend; state checks were more reliable than WebGPU screenshots.
The fixed-step gameplay simulation, controller-first UI and host-authoritative co-op, including standalone pairing and the Hub lifecycle.
Coordinating asynchronous renderer startup, native animation, Rapier sensor collisions and network snapshots across local, remote and headless-authority roles.
Built-in device-loss recovery with actionable renderer startup diagnostics.
promptFeedback: The specific source, controller-first constraints, single-file deliverable and required testable attract/dev modes gave the game a clear shape.
The no-internet-research request coexists with a required online integration URL; I treated reading that supplied protocol and downloading dependencies as implementation rather than source research.
Delivering a polished complete arcade loop and several multiplayer transports in a single offline-capable HTML.
State whether standalone online play needs a hosted signaling service; this version uses manual WebRTC pairing alongside AI Hub.

aiHub.name: Demon Encore
aiHub.description: An ink-lined arcade shooter with swooping demons, splitting hatchlings and a crown-wearing headliner. Phase through crossfire, graze bolts to charge an Encore, and hold the sky solo or in shared co-op.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / A D / arrows / mouse / touch drag; fire: R2 or Cross / Space or click / touch auto; dash: R1 or Circle / Shift or right click / two fingers; Encore: L1 or Square / E / double tap; pause: Options / Esc.
